cards.front: At 35 weeks, a multiparous woman has an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy and wants vaginal birth. With reassuring assessment and no contraindications, the obstetric team plans external cephalic version from [___].
cards.context:
Many babies turn spontaneously before term. For a multiparous woman, the usual starting point is 37 weeks rather than an early preterm attempt.

Version requires informed consent, fetal assessment and facilities for urgent caesarean birth if complications occur.

cards.front: PPROM (preterm prelabour rupture of membranes) diagnosis: history of fluid gush + sterile speculum examination showing pooling of amniotic fluid; avoid [___] vaginal exam (raises infection risk, shortens latency).
cards.context:
The 'no digital VE in PPROM' rule is a key safety rule: each digital exam introduces vaginal flora into the cervix and through ruptured membranes, raising chorioamnionitis risk + shortening latency by hours.

Use sterile speculum instead — visualises cervix + pooling without entering the os. If labour established and you need dilatation, a single careful digital exam may be unavoidable — document the indication.

'Gush' history is sensitive but not specific (urinary incontinence, discharge, amniocentesis leak can mimic) — confirm with speculum + IGFBP-1/PAMG-1 if uncertain.

cards.front: Fetal growth restriction with relative head sparing and a small abdominal circumference classically suggests [___].
cards.context:
Head sparing with a small abdominal circumference classically suggests later placental disease. The pattern guides assessment but does not establish the cause.

Symmetric restriction suggests an early or chronic insult: aneuploidy, congenital infection or smoking/drug exposure. It is not specific for aneuploidy.

cards.front: A positive pregnancy test does not remove surgical causes of pelvic pain, including [___].
cards.context:
The acute pelvic-pain list places appendicitis and colitis beside ectopic pregnancy and pelvic infection. A pregnancy test is done because she is of childbearing age.

Colitis and ovarian pathology stay on that list. Pregnancy is assessed at the same time as those non-obstetric causes, not instead of them.

cards.front: Australian stillbirth rate is approximately 7 per 1000 births; about [___]% are considered potentially preventable.
cards.context:
Australia's stillbirth rate (~7 per 1000) has barely moved in two decades despite gains elsewhere in maternal-fetal medicine.

The 20-week / 400g threshold (Australian/AIHW definition; WHO uses ≥28 weeks / ≥1000g for international comparison) separates stillbirth from late miscarriage.

That a fifth to a third are potentially preventable is the rationale behind the Safer Baby Bundle — the flat rate reflects missed modifiable risks (FGR, smoking, supine sleep), not an unavoidable floor.

cards.front: Active management of the third stage of labour gives oxytocin 10 IU IM at or soon after birth of the [___] shoulder.
cards.context:
Active management of the third stage is oxytocin 10 IU IM at or soon after birth of the anterior shoulder, then controlled cord traction once the placenta has separated.

Compared with physiological management it reduces blood loss, severe PPH and transfusion.

Give it shortly after birth: Australian guidance reports no significant PPH difference between giving it before or after the placenta, so a late dose is no reason to omit it.

cards.front: [___] uterus is blood infiltration of the myometrium from severe placental abruption, causing uterine atony and PPH; risk of DIC from disrupted decidua.
cards.context:
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is the visual signature of severe placental abruption at caesarean — blood has dissected from retroplacental haematoma into myometrium, producing a purple, bruised uterus.

Severe abruption also releases tissue factor + procoagulants from disrupted decidua → DIC (consumptive coagulopathy: falling platelets, falling fibrinogen, raised D-dimer, prolonged INR/APTT).

Hysterectomy may be unavoidable if uterotonics, B-Lynch, UAE all fail.

cards.front: The single biggest risk factor for postpartum endometritis is route of birth: [___]; treatment is amoxicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole.
cards.context:
Endometritis is polymicrobial bacterial infection of the endometrium + adjacent decidua.

Presentation: fever ≥38°C, lower abdominal/uterine tenderness, malodorous lochia, raised WCC.

Consider differentials (wound infection, retained products, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis).

cards.front: Neonatal hypoglycaemia: BGL <[___] mmol/L; at-risk groups (LGA, IDM, SGA, preterm) need BGL check at 1-2 hours; symptomatic → IV dextrose 10%.
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia (BGL <2.6 mmol/L) is the commonest metabolic problem in newborns.

Screen at-risk infants: BGL at 1-2 h then before feeds for ≥12-24 h.

cards.front: cystic fibrosis (IRT marker) has been part of Australian newborn screening since the 1980s-90s; the genuinely recent additions are SMA (SMN1 deletion — gene therapy is disease-modifying) and [___] (TREC assay — early stem cell transplant).
cards.context:
CF (~1:2500) has been part of the Australian newborn screening panel since the 1980s-90s: raised IRT → DNA test for CFTR mutations; early dx enables prophylactic enzyme replacement, salt supplementation, surveillance.

SMA and SCID are the genuinely recent additions to the panel.

SMA (~1:10,000): SMN1 deletion by PCR; presymptomatic gene therapy (onasemnogene) is disease-modifying and most effective when given before symptom onset, not a guaranteed cure.

cards.front: The 0–10 score assessed at 1 and 5 minutes to summarise a newborn's condition is the [___] score.
cards.context: A 0–10 snapshot of newborn condition at 1 and 5 minutes (Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration). It describes the baby — it does NOT guide resuscitation, which proceeds on breathing/heart rate in real time.

cards.front: For most of the menstrual cycle, estradiol [___] the release of LH and FSH.
cards.context:
For most of the cycle, estradiol holds back GnRH, LH and FSH, the same way thyroid hormone holds back TSH.

The exception is the late follicular phase: a high estradiol level held for about two days flips the pituitary into positive feedback and the LH surge follows.

cards.front: The BMI threshold defining obesity before pregnancy is [___] kg/m².
cards.context:
Higher BMI is associated with gestational diabetes, hypertensive disease, thrombosis and stillbirth. The size of each association varies with BMI severity and the population studied.

The threshold classifies BMI; it does not create a sudden biological change in risk. Avoid treating one relative-risk multiplier as universal for every woman with obesity.

cards.front: Newborn metabolic screening includes [___] (preventable intellectual disability with diet) and MCAD deficiency (hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, prevent fasting).
cards.context:
Two metabolic conditions on the Guthrie panel: phenylketonuria (PKU), where diet prevents phenylalanine neurotoxicity, and MCAD deficiency, where avoiding fasting prevents hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

MCAD (~1:15,000) impairs fatty acid oxidation, so patients can't generate ketones during fasting/illness — presents with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: Hypertension in pregnancy is SBP ≥140 and/or DBP ≥90 mmHg on [___] occasions ≥4 h apart (or a single reading ≥160/110).
cards.context:
The pregnancy threshold (140/90) sits below the general adult treatment threshold because mild hypertension matters more here.

Placental perfusion is pressure-dependent, and untreated HTN drives pre-eclampsia, abruption, and IUGR.

Timing reframes the same number. Before 20 weeks, 140/90 is chronic HTN (secondary-cause workup); after 20 weeks it is gestational HTN or pre-eclampsia, triggering an end-organ screen (urinalysis, LFTs, FBC, creatinine).

cards.front: Pulmonary vascular resistance can fall as the lung expands, even when the inflating gas is [___].
cards.context:
The first breath drops pulmonary resistance as the lung expands. The same fall is seen when the gas contains no oxygen.

That points to vessels opening as the lung expands. Improved oxygenation also reverses hypoxic vasoconstriction.

cards.front: Ipsilateral ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis form the classic triad of [___].
cards.context:
The classic triad is ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis on the affected side. These reflect interrupted sympathetic supply; sweating changes may be difficult to appreciate in a newborn.

With lower brachial plexus injury, ipsilateral pupil and eyelid changes suggest associated T1 sympathetic involvement. Horner syndrome is not required for a diagnosis of Klumpke palsy.
